title: Ravana's wounded pride
hook: the king of Lanka hears the news, makes a plan, and is talked out of it on the first try
carry: ahankara: the pride that dussehra burns
tomorrow: Rama is dharma with a body

segments.voice: Yesterday: in a muhurta and a half, Rama alone defeated Khara's army and kept his word to the sages, but Akampana escaped. Vachan: Rama keeps his word, whatever it costs.

Until now, the Ramayana has spoken of Ravana without showing him. Now the story crosses the sea, into his city. Akampana arrives in Lanka shaking and tells the king of the rakshasas everything: Janasthana is empty, Khara and Dushana are dead, fourteen thousand lie on the field, and one man did it. Ravana's first response is rage. Who is this man? I'll burn him. And Akampana says: you can't beat him. But I know how you can hurt him.
screen: `ACROSS THE SEA, IN LANKA.` → `ONE MAN DID THIS.` → `I KNOW HOW TO HURT HIM.`

segments.voice: Akampana's idea is cold. Rama has a wife, Sita, and no woman is her equal in beauty, he says. Carry her off, and Rama will die of grief without a single arrow. Ravana takes his chariot across the sea to Maricha, the rakshasa Rama spared years ago at Vishvamitra's sacrifice, who has lived as a kind of hermit since. Maricha says no. Whoever told you this is your enemy pretending to be your friend. Rama is a sleeping lion; don't poke him. Go home. And Ravana listens, and goes home. Then Shurpanakha arrives at his court, wounded, and she doesn't plead. She scolds him in front of everyone: what kind of king are you, lost in pleasure while one man destroys your army? Then she describes Sita, at length. The warning that worked once is about to be overruled. Here's how Hindus read Ravana. He isn't a fool. In the tradition he's learned, mighty, a great devotee of Shiva. What brings him down is ahankara, the ego, the I that has to be the biggest. Good advice reached his mind once. But with his pride stung in public, the ego takes the wheel. That's why every Dussehra, in towns across India and beyond, a giant Ravana goes up in flames at the end of the Ramlila, and many teachers say what burns is ahankara, his and ours. Some read his ten heads as the many faces of pride and craving.
screen: `TAKE HIS WIFE, AKAMPANA SAYS.` · `MARICHA: DON'T POKE THE LION.` · `SHURPANAKHA SHAMES THE KING.` · `AHANKARA: THE EGO.` · then, large: `WHAT DUSSEHRA BURNS.`

segments.voice: Many Hindus bow, or touch an elder's feet, and teachers say the bow is the ego lowering its head. Fold your hands at your heart and bow your head a little. If you pray, bow to God; if not, bow to the day. Recall a time your pride was stung and you wanted to prove something. Breathe out slowly, and let the head stay low a moment longer.
Ravana, 'the one who makes others cry out': the learned king of Lanka, turned back by Maricha, then shamed into the plan by Shurpanakha.
Carry this: ahankara, the pride that Dussehra burns. Maricha's no held, until Shurpanakha spoke. That's day five hundred sixty-five.

screen: `DAY 565 COUNTS.` → `AHANKARA: THE PRIDE THAT DUSSEHRA BURNS.` → `TOMORROW: RAMA IS DHARMA WITH A BODY.`

howItsDone: At Dussehra, effigies of Ravana are burned at the end of Ramlila in India and beyond, and many teachers say what burns is ahankara, the ego; recitations that tell this part in full keep Maricha's first refusal.

fork.setup: you're Ravana. you took good advice and went home. now your sister shames you before the whole court. what would beat ahankara?
options: hold to the good advice, even if the court thinks you're weak.
prove her wrong: do something big, fast.
fork.reveal: Ravana lets stung pride overrule Maricha's warning. Hindus call it ahankara, the ego taking the wheel, and burn its picture at Dussehra.

original.note: Sanskrit rāvaṇa: traditionally explained as 'the one who makes others cry out,' the king of the rakshasas in Lanka.

what a scholar hears: Aranya 31 gives Akampana's plan and Maricha's first refusal; Aranya 32–34 Shurpanakha's rebuke of a negligent king.

chat.meaning: Ravana took Maricha's advice and went home, until Shurpanakha shamed him in court. Hindus call what took over ahankara, the ego, and burn Ravana's effigy at Dussehra.

tie.story: Ravana took Maricha's warning and went home, until his sister shamed him before his court and his pride overruled it.

Ravana.meaning: the king of the rakshasas, who rules Lanka

Akampana.meaning: the rakshasa who escaped Rama's battle

Maricha.meaning: the rakshasa Rama once spared, now living as a hermit

Vishvamitra.meaning: the sage whose sacrifice young Rama once guarded

Lanka.meaning: Ravana's island city across the sea

ahankara.meaning: the ego, the sense of I that wants to be biggest

Dussehra.meaning: the festival of Rama's victory, when Ravana's effigy burns

sangeet.meaning: the music and dance night before a wedding
